dateRangeHelp: **Filters the export to a date range.** XPorter opens an X search tab and scrolls it to collect the posts — **keep that tab open until the export finishes.**
profileFeedHelp: **All matches X's All feed and is recommended:** original posts, quotes, replies, and complete author threads. Posts uses X's Posts feed and excludes replies. **Quotes are posts, not replies; reposts follow the separate switch.**
includeBookmarkReplyContextHelp: **For saved replies, fetches the post being answered and stores it inside the same bookmark record.** Parent posts do not increase the bookmark count. XPorter batches their IDs, but pages containing replies still need extra X requests. Deleted, private, or blocked posts may remain unavailable.
includeBookmarkArticlesHelp: **Keeps the title, URL, and all Article text returned by X, including Articles inside quoted or replied-to posts.** Some Articles expose only a preview; XPorter preserves exactly what X returns.
embedPhotosHelp: **XLSX only. Downloads photos from X while the file is being saved and places them on a separate Media sheet.** Several photos from a post, quote, or replied-to post are kept as separate rows. This can make saving much slower and the workbook much larger; large exports may be split into several XLSX files. Videos remain links.
quantityLimitHelp: **How many posts (or users) to collect before the export stops.** Example: 500 stops at 500 posts. **For Posts, X usually exposes only about 3,200 of the most recent items, even when a profile shows more.** XPorter cannot bypass this X availability limit. Followers and Following have different limits.
postsExportSpeedHelp: **Controls Posts and Bookmarks exports. The five presets wait about 2, 3, 4, 7, or 12 seconds between requests in the typical fallback path. Standard is the recommended 4-second balance.** If X's live quota runs low, XPorter pauses until it resets instead of risking a failed export. **⚠️ Custom lets you set your own pause between requests plus a longer break every N requests.**
userListsExportSpeedHelp: **Controls Followers, Following, and Verified Followers exports. X gives each list endpoint a different request budget, so actual pauses vary by mode. Standard is recommended.** If the live quota runs low, XPorter safely waits for its reset. **⚠️ Custom sets a separate pause and batch break for user lists.**
aboutDesc: Free & unlimited export of X (Twitter) data to CSV, JSON, XLSX, or TXT.

errStaleQuery: X API changed — retrying with fresh data...
errRepliesUnavailable: The Replies tab is temporarily unavailable

postsOnlyFallbackComplete: Export completed from Posts only — replies were not included

autoExpireHelp: **Auto-deletes saved export data after the set number of hours** to free space. Your past exports stay in the history list, but old ones **may no longer be downloadable.**
feedStatsDescription: Quietly saves the posts you scroll past on X, so you can export them later. Stays on your device, sends no extra requests.

largeExportCsvTip: CSV is recommended for the largest exports because it uses less memory.

update151Body: Export personal Bookmarks to CSV, JSON, XLSX, or TXT with quoted posts, replied-to context, Articles, metrics, and optional embedded photos. Files now omit columns or fields that are empty throughout, while TXT labels make every metric's owner clear. Pacing, retries, resume handling, and popup help and layout are also more reliable.
update150Title: Richer account data and safer replies
update150Body: Added public “About this Account” fields for user lists, fuller profile context in post files, quoted-post and Article data, separate pacing for posts and user lists, and protected X request compatibility. Replies use a dedicated combined timeline with a safe fallback, while rate-limit pauses show a live retry countdown and resumable progress.
update1411Body: Large downloads are split into safe numbered parts, AI-friendly TXT was added for posts, and resume now keeps export filters while applying the latest pacing settings.
update148Body: The export engine was split into focused modules, interrupted jobs became reliably resumable, and post and user-list parsing gained stronger validation and persistence.
detailLocalBody: Everything runs inside your browser. There are no XPorter servers, no account, and no analytics or tracking. Your data goes straight from X into the file you download — it never passes through us.
detailSessionBody: XPorter reads the same public data you already see when you're logged in, using the X session that's already in your browser. It never asks for your password and never stores your login.
detailExportsBody: Posts, followers, following, and verified followers. Post exports include the full engagement metrics — views, likes, reposts, replies, quotes, and bookmarks — plus dates, links, media, and hashtags.
detailFormatsBody: Pick the format that fits your workflow: CSV for any spreadsheet, XLSX for Excel, JSON for developers, or TXT for AI. Files are built locally and download straight to your device.
detailDatesBody: Export posts from a specific time window. Date-range exports open an X search tab and scroll it automatically to gather matching posts — just keep that tab open until it finishes.
detailResumeBody: Progress is saved as the export runs, so you can pause, close the popup, or even restart your browser and continue where you left off. XPorter also paces its requests to respect X's limits and avoid temporary blocks.
exportModeHelp:
What each export mode collects:
**📝 Posts** — all of the profile's posts (tweets, replies, reposts and quotes) with their full stats.
**🔖 Bookmarks** — posts saved by your current X account. This mode opens the personal Bookmarks page and does not accept another username. X can change this private feed, so some data may be missing or temporarily unavailable.
**👥 Followers** — the accounts that follow this profile.
**➡️ Following** — the accounts this profile follows.
**✓ Verified Followers** — only followers that have a verified (blue) checkmark.
rateBody: XPorter is **free** and **unlimited**. I'm always adding new features and fixing bugs. If it's helping you, please leave **5 stars**. It really supports the project and helps others find it.
aboutSourceSub: The full source code is on GitHub — read exactly what runs in your browser. Questions, ideas and pull requests are always welcome: help XPorter grow.
aboutSafetySub: To X, an export looks like you reading the page: XPorter uses your own logged-in session, only reads data you can already see, and paces its requests like normal browsing — with built-in pauses that respect X's limits. It never posts, follows, likes, or changes anything on your account.
aboutAccountSpeedHelp: Controls how many “About this Account” requests run at the same time. Standard uses 5 accounts per batch. Higher values are faster but more likely to hit X rate limits or a temporary restriction. Turtle is safest. Custom accepts 1 to 50.
aboutAccountRetriesHelp: How many one-minute retries XPorter makes after X rejects an About request. A successful request resets the count. Choose up to 1,440 for up to one day of retrying.
aboutEnableRiskBody:
⚡ Without this option, XPorter exports normal profile data much faster.

Enable it only if you need these extra fields: account country/region, Premium start date, connection source, affiliated account, and username-change history.

🐢 It makes up to one extra profile request per user. The same export can be dramatically slower, X may start rate-limiting after roughly 50 profiles, and account restrictions are possible. This experimental mode is not recommended for routine exports.
aboutRetryRiskBody:
⏳ This value allows more than one hour of one-minute retries after X rejects an About request. It may keep an export running longer, but it also sends more repeated requests and can increase the risk of temporary account restrictions.

Use a high value only if you accept that risk. XPorter cannot guarantee that the export will finish.
includeAboutAccountDetailsHelp:
Adds public “About this Account” data: account location, Premium date, connection source, affiliated account, and username-change history.

⚠️ **This feature is much more demanding:** XPorter makes up to one extra request for every user, so exports can be much slower. 500 users can mean up to 500 extra requests and may hit X rate limits or temporary restrictions. Enable it only when needed and use a slower speed.
localizeHeadersHelp: **Translates the CSV and XLSX column headers into your language.** Turn it off to keep the original English headers; they work best with scripts and spreadsheet templates. JSON keys always stay English.
